title: cart_total sums floats with no rounding, so totals shown to the customer carry float noise
evidence: Executed in the workspace: cart_total([0.1, 0.2]) returns 0.30000000000000004; cart_total([19.99, 5.01, 0.1]) returns 25.099999999999998; notify(sender, that total) sends 'Your total is 0.30000000000000004'. apply_discount rounds to 2 places (line 11) but cart_total does not, so the two money functions disagree. Every test uses ints only (tests/test_cart.py:7-23, tests/test_helpers_ok.py:10-29), so nothing covers decimal prices.
failing_case: A cart with prices [19.99, 5.01, 0.1] gives 25.099999999999998. notify() puts that string in the customer message. Comparing it to an expected 25.10 total also fails.
remediation: Use Decimal or integer cents for prices, and quantize the total to 2 places in cart_total. Add a test with decimal prices.

requirement.why: a cart total is money; apply_discount already rounds to 2 places, which shows 2-decimal amounts are intended

quote: @pytest.mark.skip(reason="bounds are checked in the integration suite until the rewrite lands")
title: The only test of the upper discount bound is skipped, so an off-by-one at 100/101 passes every test
evidence: Mutation traced against src/cart.py:9. Changing `percent > 100` to `percent > 101` (or `>= 100`) leaves all active tests green: the only test that passes 101 is the skipped test_discount_bounds. Other raising tests use -1, 200 and 500 (tests/test_helpers_ok.py:19, 34, 68), which still raise under the mutation. No test calls apply_discount(100, 100). The skip names an integration suite that is not in this change and gives no date or ticket.
failing_case: Mutate cart.py:9 to `percent > 101`. apply_discount(100, 101) then returns -1.0, a negative price. All active tests still pass.
remediation: Un-skip test_discount_bounds. Add apply_discount(100, 100) == 0 and apply_discount(100, 0) == 100 as boundary tests. If a skip stays, name a ticket and a condition.

requirement.why: the skipped test and the error message 'percent must be between 0 and 100' state the bound

title: Helper named `test` is collected by pytest as a test and errors on a missing fixture `name`
evidence: pytest's default python_functions is the prefix 'test', and 'test' starts with 'test', so a module-level function `test(name)` is collected. Its parameter `name` is not a fixture, so setup reports 'fixture name not found' as an ERROR. The file's header says none of its content should be flagged, yet this one entry makes the file's run red. Traced: pytest is not installed in the workspace and I did not install it.
failing_case: Run `pytest tests/test_helpers_ok.py`. Collection includes tests/test_helpers_ok.py::test, which errors with `fixture 'name' not found`. The run exits non-zero even when every real test passes.
remediation: Rename the helper (for example `deco_factory`) so it does not match the test prefix, or move it out of the test module.
